hypotheses.title: GDR measured geothermometry (wellspring chemistry, T >= 150/180/200 C) as a *removal prior* on the 0.2708 base emission
layers: external: gdr.openei.org files/1391/wellspringdata.gdb.zip (1,014 chemistry rows, 184 geothermometer sites)
19 official bands only as a corroboration filter
hypotheses.signature: each spring's Na-K-Ca / silica geothermometer temperature placed on the 100 m grid, blurred by the 300 m kernel, and used to *delete* dots from the base emission
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: 15 of the 53 sites above 150 C lie >3 km from any mapped trace, so a geothermometer anomaly is evidence of a fault the catalogue has not mapped
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: H18-5 'thermal-anchor linking' was registered by the 16GEMSDOE operator with the same premise and was never built; this arm builds it. No arm in this repo has ever used measured geochemistry.
hypotheses.expected_dti: as an ADDITION arm: FALSIFIED - measured credit/dot 0.0022-0.0054 against the live break-even bar tau_live = 0.05416 (10-25x too expensive)
hypotheses.cost: low (one CSV + IDW surface + a threshold)
hypotheses.data_status: VERIFIED OBTAINABLE: gdr.openei.org/submissions/1391, official, CC BY 4.0, DOI 10.15121/1881483, file wellspringdata.gdb.zip; already materialised in data/raw/external/
hypotheses.status: FALSIFIED as an addition arm (H33-1-P600A1800: +0.002639 LM, 2/4 folds, 0.00541 credit/dot). Retained only as a possible pruning prior; NOT slot-eligible.

hypotheses.title: Catalogue-flank buffer B = 2 (200 m) on the 0.2708 base: a pure removal arm with a live-anchored credit-loss budget
layers: the group's best live-scored emission (GEMS28-H27-4-R1-SOLO-D2.8, 40,199 dots)
hypotheses.signature: delete every dot within B pixels of the published catalogue; no transform, no new data, no geometry change - one mechanism only
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: the hidden truth is drawn from faults *not* in the catalogue, so mass spent within 100-200 m of a mapped line can never earn round-2 credit; B = 1 was the only value the group ever tested live and it produced the 0.2708 record
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: the group tested B = 1 live (0.2600 -> 0.2708) and never anything else; B = 2 is a new, non-obvious operating point that the live-anchored inversion shows is still inside the credit-loss budget
hypotheses.expected_dti: +0.004870 live-mirror, 4/4 folds, safety factor 2.08, projected live 0.2747 (a MODEL, not a score)
hypotheses.cost: very low (one distance transform + a threshold)
hypotheses.data_status: all inputs already in the repository; no external data needed
hypotheses.status: WINNER. H33-2-B2 is the shipped primary: 37,654 dots, LM-cal 0.267921 vs base 0.263051, off-catalogue credit 58.6 units against a budget of 125.1. Slot-eligible.

hypotheses.title: 2 m temperature-probe thermal grid (GDR 1391 resource '2m Temperature Probes') as a *thin* anomaly mask, added only where it is corroborated by at least two independent official layers
layers: official bands 1-19 as the corroboration filter
catalogue buffer B = 2 as the domain restriction
hypotheses.signature: a shallow thermal anomaly map; only cells where the probe temperature and an independent geophysical layer agree are eligible for emission
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: shallow conductive heat is the physical driver of hydrothermal alteration and fault permeability, and the 2 m probe network samples ground the geophysical grid cannot resolve
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: features.py has 35 channels and NO thermal channel; no arm has ever used a measured temperature field. Requires the external download, so it is a registered-but-unbuilt arm.
hypotheses.expected_dti: unmeasured. Expected to be cheaper than H33-1 (a *mask*, not an IDW surface) but still subject to the same tau_live bar
hypotheses.cost: medium (one download + a join + a two-layer corroboration rule)
hypotheses.data_status: VERIFIED OBTAINABLE and OFFICIAL: gdr.openei.org/submissions/1391, CC BY 4.0, DOI 10.15121/1881483, resource 2m_temperature_probe_INGENIOUS_regional_data.zip (1.03 MB). Not yet downloaded to this checkout.
hypotheses.status: registered; not yet built; no slot

hypotheses.title: Paleo geothermal features (GDR 1391 resource 'Paleo Geothermal Features') as a *geological prior* for the tip and step-over neighbourhoods of range-front faults
hypotheses.signature: a Quaternary/paleo geothermal feature layer (silica sinter, travertine, tufa, spring mounds) marking where the crust has already leaked fluid; these sit on active structures and are largely absent from the fault catalogue
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: a paleo-geothermal feature is evidence of a *present-day* permeable structure; the INGENIOUS fault compilation does not carry that attribute, so the layer points at faults the catalogue has not mapped
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: no arm has used any geothermal-feature vector. It is a *prior over where to emit*, not a detector, so it cannot be confused with the detector-field family (H33-5).
hypotheses.expected_dti: unmeasured; expected small on the public split, unbounded on the final round if the expert panel verifies a new fault
hypotheses.cost: medium (one download + rasterise + neighbourhood emission rule)
hypotheses.data_status: VERIFIED OBTAINABLE and OFFICIAL: gdr.openei.org/submissions/1391, CC BY 4.0, DOI 10.15121/1881483, resource paleo_geothermal_regional.zip (82.04 kB). Not yet downloaded.
hypotheses.status: registered; not yet built; no slot

hypotheses.title: Detector-field tip / step-over extension: grow the existing ridge field at the propagation tip and at releasing-bend step-overs of detected structures
layers: the 35-channel detector field built from the 19 official bands
hypotheses.signature: skeletonise the ridge field, find its endpoints and its releasing/ restraining bends, and extend a short arm at each; the physical target is fault-tip damage zones and step-over relay ramps
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: a fault tip is by definition the *end* of a mapped trace, so anything predicted there is off-catalogue by construction
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: the repo has ridge NMS (H32-A..D) and Poisson thinning, but no tip/step-over geometry operator at all
hypotheses.expected_dti: FALSIFIED as an addition arm: +0.001870 LM, 3/4 folds, 0.00767 credit/dot vs tau_live = 0.05416 (7x too expensive)
hypotheses.cost: medium (skeleton + Hessian ridge response + a short-extension rule)
hypotheses.status: FALSIFIED as an addition arm (H33-5-P300A900). Not slot-eligible. Do not re-propose as an addition arm.

hypotheses.title: Post-catalogue coseismic surface ruptures (Monte Cristo Range 2020 Mw 6.5 and the pre-2020 historical rupture set) as high-precision line targets
layers: USGS/NBMG 2020 MCRE surface-rupture traces (Dee et al., NBMG TR-190; SRL 92(2A))
19 official bands only as a corroboration filter
hypotheses.signature: exact mapped rupture polylines rasterised on the 100 m grid (no transform, no detection: the geometry is the measurement)
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: the competition labels are the pre-2020 USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue; the MCRE rupture occurred on 2020-05-15 in *largely unmapped parts of the Candelaria fault* and is by construction absent from a pre-2020 catalogue, while being real, published and trivially verifiable by the expert panel
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: the group has emission, packing, Euler, slip-tendency, hydrothermal and catalogue-difference families, but no arm built on post-catalogue coseismic ruptures; H41/SGMC arms used *catalogue* vectors, which cannot contain a fault that post-dates the catalogue
hypotheses.expected_dti: 0.000 to +0.02 on the public split (single 28 km trace, ~2 % of the group's emitted mass); unbounded on the final round because the expert panel can verify the fault and add it to the expanded label set
hypotheses.cost: low (one vector download + rasterise + geometric thinning)
hypotheses.data_status: source located and documented (see registry/sources.json); obtainability from this sandbox is blocked (sciencebase.gov unknown-host), so the arm ships as a registered hypothesis with a CI fetch step, not as a claimed result
hypotheses.status: registered; not yet measured; no slot

hypotheses.title: Catalogue-difference emission: faults mapped in newer state datasets but absent from the competition labels, gated by a geophysical corroboration filter
layers: NBMG Qfaults-INGENIOUS v2 vectors (1,179 features in footprint)
hypotheses.signature: distance-to-nearest-newer-catalogue-trace < 2 px AND ridge/curvature corroboration on the detrended DEM
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: the hidden test set is *newly identified* faults: a newer state mapping that post-dates the national catalogue is, by construction, a sample of exactly that population
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: the group's H41/SGMC arms emitted catalogue vectors *without* a geophysical gate and both lost their secondary proxy; here the gate is the corroboration filter inside `emission.py` (credit bar), and the arm is scored at matched mass
hypotheses.data_status: vectors are hash-pinned in the group's own mirrors (GEMSDOE24) and reachable from this sandbox via the GitHub API
hypotheses.status: registered; partially measured (see evidence/)

hypotheses.title: Adaptive credit-bar emission: stop the emission where the marginal expected credit per unit mass falls below 0.2 x DTI (the metric's own break-even)
hypotheses.signature: greedy maximum-expected-coverage packing of the field under the official triangular kernel with an *adaptive* stopping rule
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: not a geological hypothesis but the decision rule for every other one: it removes the fixed-count budget that the group's sweeps showed to be family-limited and replaces it with the metric's analytic bar
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: H37-1 fixed the packing objective but kept a matched *count*; here the count is an output, and the same rule gives the discovery-weighted variant used for the two-round objective
hypotheses.expected_dti: measured on the blocked holdout (see evidence/holdout_run1.json)
hypotheses.status: measured on the blocked holdout

hypotheses.title: Two-round discovery option value: lower the emission bar for candidates whose verification is likely, because the same file is re-scored against the expanded label set
layers: published fault evidence for the verification prior
hypotheses.signature: objective DTI_1 + rho * DTI_2 with rho set by the prize structure ($50k initial round vs $250k final round); the effective bar becomes 0.2 x DTI / (1 + rho)
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: the initial-round label set is deliberately incomplete, so public-LB maximisation under-prices true-but-unlabelled faults; the metric's alpha = 0.2 (false positives four times cheaper than false negatives) is the organisers' own statement that they want such predictions
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: no prior arm, gate or budget in the group's record uses the two-round structure; every promotion bar to date is round-1 only
hypotheses.expected_dti: raises the *expected* final-round score; cannot be measured on any local holdout and must be reasoned about from the published prize structure
hypotheses.cost: none (a change in the decision rule)
hypotheses.status: implemented as A3 in the holdout ladder and as `rho` in `bo.slot_gate`

hypotheses.title: Cross-scale drainage-network organisation (stream-power / knickpoint residuals) as an independent lineament family
layers: 1 m / 10 m 3DEP DEM from the official link table (1m_DEM_links.csv)
hypotheses.signature: chi-profile and knickpoint residuals along the channel network; aligned knickpoints across a basin trace a fault that displaces the network but has no preserved scarp
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: targets faults in alluvium/valley fill with no topographic scarp, i.e. exactly the class a surface-mapping catalogue lacks
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: the group ran a drainage arm (H43) that *passed* its primary screen and was withheld on a secondary proxy; it was built on the 100 m detrended surface, and a 1 m/10 m channel network with a chi transform is a different measurement
hypotheses.data_status: the official link table is mirrored in the group's repo (`data/dem_links.json`, sha256 8804dbff8754...); tile fetch needs CI egress
hypotheses.status: registered; not run (cost), no slot

hypotheses.title: Basement-step lineaments gated by surface quiescence
layers: depth_to_base_surf (organizer: 'Depth to basement surface - thickness of sedimentary cover')
hypotheses.signature: multi-scale ridge extraction on the GRADIENT-MAGNITUDE RIDGE (Hessian ridge, 3 scales) of sediment-cover thickness, then skeletonised: a fault-block boundary is a STEP in cover thickness, so the boundary is the crest line of the gradient field, not the gradient blob. Gated by LOW surface expression (small det_elev_slope, small surface curvature).
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: a Quaternary surface-fault catalogue records what is exposed; a block boundary under thick basin fill has no surface trace and therefore cannot be in it. The quiescence gate is the discriminator: it removes exactly the population the catalogue already contains (faults with scarps).
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: features.py has only depth_grad = smoothed |grad band15|, a first-derivative magnitude. It never extracts the ridge line of that gradient, never uses the cover-thickness VALUE as a concealment weight, never applies a surface-quiescence gate, and never works at more than one scale. The sibling repository's concealment prior used SGMC map-unit polygons, not the official cover-thickness raster.
hypotheses.expected_dti: highest of the five: it changes WHERE mass goes rather than how it is packed
hypotheses.cost: low (one official band, already on disk; no new data)
hypotheses.status: registered; NOT validated; no slot requested

hypotheses.title: Seismicity lineament coupling
layers: det_elev, det_elev_slope as the corroborating surface witness
hypotheses.signature: anisotropic ridge / coherence maxima of the seismicity-density field (structure tensor -> coherence + orientation, then non-maximum suppression along the minor axis at two scales), required to coincide with a curvature inflection in the detrended surface. A line of hypocentres is a fault plane; a density blob is not.
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: instrumental seismicity is a DYNAMIC inventory. Blind faults, creeping faults, and faults whose slip rate is too low to have preserved a Quaternary scarp still rupture small earthquakes; a geomorphic catalogue records only the last of those three.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: features.py carries bands 10 and 16 ONLY as raw columns; no derived channel uses them, no registry arm uses seismicity, and there is no ridge, coherence or orientation transform on either band anywhere in the tree.
hypotheses.expected_dti: moderate: coverage gain concentrated in basin interiors the field currently under-serves
hypotheses.cost: low (bands on disk; free USGS ComCat API optional for hypocentral depths)
hypotheses.data_status: bands on disk; ComCat obtainability untested
hypotheses.status: registered; NOT validated; no slot requested

hypotheses.title: Tilt-angle (TDR) zero-crossing magnetic edge lineaments
layers: tc (organizer: 'Tilt angle or total curvature - magnetic field derivative FOR EDGE DETECTION')
hypotheses.signature: the ZERO-CROSSING CONTOUR of the tilt angle, not its magnitude: the tilt derivative is the standard depth-independent locator for a magnetic contact, whereas the magnitude peaks wander with source depth. Paired with tmi_vg as an independent witness, rejecting where the two disagree.
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: TDR edges respond to SUBSURFACE magnetisation contrasts irrespective of exposure, so they locate contacts under cover and contacts with no topographic expression.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: features.py derives tmi_edge = |grad band14| and rtp_edge = |grad band2| but never touches band 6 or band 9. Band 6 is the layer the organizers describe as being for edge detection and it has NO derived channel in this repo. Measured: tmi_edge correlates with official band 3 at rho = +0.9330 (IR-32-REDUND-01), so the repo spends a channel recomputing a supplied layer while leaving the purpose-built edge layer unused.
hypotheses.expected_dti: moderate: strongest where magnetic coverage exists
hypotheses.status: registered; NOT validated; no slot requested

hypotheses.title: GNSS-derived full 2-D strain tensor -> principal-axis anisotropic matched filter
layers: official bands INSUFFICIENT: geod_2ndinv, geod_shearrate and geod_dilaterate are three scalars of a tensor; orientation is not recoverable from them
external: Nevada Geodetic Laboratory MIDAS velocity field (http://geodesy.unr.edu/) and/or EarthScope/UNAVCO GNSS velocity products (https://www.unavco.org/)
hypotheses.signature: reconstruct the full 2-D strain-rate tensor from GNSS velocities, take its principal extensional axis, and use that azimuth as the orientation prior of an oriented matched filter (a fault strikes near-perpendicular to sigma_3), tuned per pixel rather than isotropically.
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: orientation predicts WHICH WAY a missing fault must run, so the search can be steered to the mechanically favoured strike where the topographic expression is ambiguous.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: no arm in this repo uses the orientation of the geodetic tensor, because it is not in the supplied data.
hypotheses.data_status: NOT OBTAINED and NOT VERIFIED as obtainable from this sandbox; per the standing brief a candidate needing external data must have its source checked as obtainable BEFORE being proposed as viable, so this entry is ranked and explicitly NOT proposed as ready to run
hypotheses.status: registered; data obtainability unverified; no slot requested

hypotheses.title: Metre-scale scarp matched filter from the official 1 m DEM link table
layers: external: 1 m / 10 m 3DEP DEM tiles from the official 1m_DEM_links.csv
hypotheses.signature: anisotropic matched filter for metre-scale scarps; a fault with less than 1 m of throw averaged over a 100 m cell is invisible in the provided grid by construction.
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: below-grid-resolution scarps are precisely the class a 1:24,000-scale surface compilation omits.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: the repo has NO LiDAR arm at all. H60-5 (chi/knickpoint residuals) is registered but was never run; this variant is a matched filter on the scarp itself, which is a cheaper and different measurement.
hypotheses.expected_dti: indirect, and the tile fetch plus hydrology is heavy on 2 vCPU
hypotheses.data_status: the official link table is mirrored in a sibling repository (sha256 8804dbff8754...); the tiles themselves were NOT obtained and their obtainability from this sandbox is unverified
hypotheses.status: registered; data obtainability unverified; no slot requested
measured (not promoted)
hypotheses.title: Multi-physics oriented-lineament consensus
hypotheses.signature: scale-normalised Hessian line response per physics x 2nd-order orientation order parameter (do independent physics agree on the strike?)
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: the catalogue is dominated by faults that were mappable in one dataset (usually topography or the existing maps); requiring multi-physics strike agreement selects the class of curvilinear structure an expert can only accept when several fields agree
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: no channel or H32 surface requires *independent* physics to agree on an orientation; features.py has per-band ridges and H32-A/C have pixel products
hypotheses.verdict: BELOW the uniform-random control on the catalogue-hidden instrument (-45%); the instrument measures agreement with the mapped catalogue, and this surface deliberately selects what the catalogue under-represents. NOT PROMOTED.

hypotheses.status: measured (not promoted)
hypotheses.title: Aligned drainage-valley chains
hypotheses.signature: valley skeleton (NMS ridge of -det_elev) x 9-px 16-direction collinearity vote, de-emphasised where det_elev_slope is high
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: faults that lack a preserved scarp still deflect and align drainage; a collinear chain of valley segments across several drainages is structural, which a single scarp-height map cannot see
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: the repo's DEM channels are all local; nothing aggregates evidence *along* a line
hypotheses.verdict: STRONGEST off-catalogue signal of the five (+49.8% over the incumbent on the SGMC-only instrument) and the WORST-class reading on the catalogue instrument (-37% vs random). The two instruments disagree in sign -- recorded as holdout drift, not as a win. NOT PROMOTED.

hypotheses.status: measured (not promoted)
hypotheses.title: En-echelon scarplet chain vote on the 1 m LiDAR scarp product
hypotheses.signature: scarplet skeleton x 11-px collinearity vote requiring contrast vs the local minimum (a scarp, not a slope break)
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: a single 1 m scarplet is noise; en-echelon collinear scarplets are what expert mappers accept as a fault, and they are below the 100 m grid
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: the repo uses the LiDAR product only as a per-pixel corroboration weight
hypotheses.verdict: Below the random control on the catalogue instrument. NOT PROMOTED.

hypotheses.status: measured (not promoted)
hypotheses.title: Long-straight conductive / basement structural boundary
hypotheses.signature: gradient magnitude x directional coherence of the gradient direction over a 3x3 window (a straight boundary, not a blobby anomaly)
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: MT conductivity and basement depth image the *subsurface*; a straight conductivity step locates a fault under cover, where a surface catalogue has nothing
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: cond_surf/depth are used as scalars or plain gradient magnitudes in features.py
hypotheses.verdict: Weakest of the five on both instruments (a 3x3 directional-coherence window is too short for a 'long-straight' criterion). NOT PROMOTED.

hypotheses.status: DATA-BLOCKED (source named, obtainability not verified here)
hypotheses.title: Sub-kilometre seismicity lineaments and nodal-plane traces from the raw earthquake catalogue
layers: ieq_n100a15 (16) and deq_n100a15 (10) would be replaced/augmented by a raw epicentre catalogue (USGS FDSN event web service) plus moment tensors
hypotheses.signature: epicentre density lineaments + focal-mechanism nodal-plane strikes as fault-plane proxies at the epicentre
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: instrumental seismicity is a dynamic inventory: blind, low-slip-rate faults light up seismically while leaving no scarp for a geomorphic map
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: the supplied seismic bands are computed on a 100 km radius; measured here, ieq is 0.9935-correlated with itself at a 3 km lag, i.e. constant at the metric's 300 m resolution
hypotheses.implementation: scripts/fetch_earthquake_catalog.sh (ready to run; NOT runnable from this sandbox: curl to earthquake.usgs.gov returns HTTP 000, browsing path HTTP 500)
hypotheses.verdict: NAMED SOURCE, obtainability NOT verified from this environment; ranked and NOT proposed as ready, per the brief's rule for externally-dependent candidates.

selection_rule.tier_1: slot-eligible under the live-anchored gate (LM-cal +margin in 4/4 quadrants over a live-scored base, safety factor >= 2.0) AND on_catalogue_pixels == 0; highest projected live DTI wins
selection_rule.tier_2: scripts/build_slot_plan.py's frozen holdout rule: beats the owner-reported 0.2600 incumbent on all three holdout instruments AND 0 on-catalogue dots
selection_rule.precedence: Tier 1 outranks Tier 2 because its instrument was validated against six known live orderings (it reproduces 0.2708 > 0.2600 at +0.011458 against live +0.0108), while Tier 2's best instrument is Spearman +0.53 at n=12 and is measured anti-monotone with live on emission questions

irregularities.statement: The historical DrivenData rejection "Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]" CANNOT be reproduced from anything currently shipped. scripts/audit_shipped.py re-reads all six GeoTIFFs in docs/downloads/ from disk and finds every one portal-legal: EPSG:32611, 3730x3292, single-band float32, 12,279,160/12,279,160 cells finite, 0 NaN, and ZERO values outside [0, 1]. The specific file behind that one upload was never obtained, so the trigger remains inferred, not proven.
irregularities.mitigation: Two mechanisms that CAN produce the condition do exist in the competition's own inputs and are measured here: (1) training_features.tif declares its nodata as -3.4028234663852886e+38 (the float32 minimum, not NaN) and 3,061 cells per band inside the 5,167,373-cell scored footprint carry that sentinel; (2) a footprint mask derived from band 1 is 1,521 cells smaller than the template footprint, stranding those cells as NaN. Both are engineered out: every shipped file is written all-finite with no nodata tag, and the writer fails closed by re-reading the bytes it just wrote. Both the NaN-outside and zero-outside encodings are published.

irregularities.statement: The group's best-scoring field (H19-5) is identically ZERO on every pixel of the given catalogue: 0 of its 121,131 positive pixels touch the 60,988 catalogue pixels. Measured here two ways (evidence/h60_2_catalogue_difference.json, registry/submission_build.json -> catalogue_px_emitted = 0).
irregularities.mitigation: Round-1 hidden truth therefore excludes the given catalogue, and mass spent on a mapped line can never earn credit. The build script removes a 1 px buffer around the catalogue from the emission domain (the first smooth-field build wasted 994 px = 2.3 % of its mass there).

irregularities.statement: The two local instruments DISAGREE about the same change, which is the drift the brief asks to chase rather than shrug off. Blocked holdout with catalogue truth: greedy surface-coverage packing beats the incumbent raster-order dot-thin at matched mass, +0.0100 mean over 4 folds (4/4 positive). Live-anchored generative truth model, official metric, paired draws: that same change is NEGATIVE, -0.0033 (0/12 draws positive).
irregularities.mitigation: Both are published. The disagreement has a mechanism, not noise: the holdout's truth is the catalogue, so it rewards covering the field surface where the catalogue is; the hidden set is scattered *around* the surface with a 1.85 px scale, so covering the surface is the wrong objective. The rule was re-derived from the second instrument (cover the scatter-smoothed density) and now measures +0.0247 (12/12 draws) over the incumbent on the catalogue-aware variant. The holdout keeps its role as a cheap screen; the model anchor decides.

irregularities.statement: The group's file named 'dotted-h19-5-d2-8' corresponds to a thinning parameter of 2.4 px in the group's own density sweep (whose peak they report at d = 2.4 px / 44,090 px), not 2.8 px. irregularities.statement: README.md and .gitignore were committed to main with UNRESOLVED MERGE-CONFLICT MARKERS: '<<<<<<< HEAD' on README line 1, '=======' line 300, '>>>>>>> origin/main' line 570; the same in .gitignore at lines 1/24/54. The repository's own front page was unreadable on GitHub, and the .gitignore rules that RE-INCLUDE the downloadable GeoTIFFs ('!docs/downloads/*.tif') sat inside the conflicted region next to a bare 'downloads/' pattern that would have excluded the docs/downloads/ directory entirely (git cannot re-include a file whose parent directory is excluded).

irregularities.statement: The repository's previously-shipped PRIMARY download, docs/downloads/gems32-h19-5-smoothmaxcov-44090.tif (sha256 2dc67f4bdb8d1bf2...), places 25,485 of its 44,090 emitted pixels (57.8%) OFF the belief field it is supposed to be packing, and scores 0.0163197 against the only real truth raster in this competition (labels.tif, 60,988 catalogue pixels) versus the incumbent's 0.1617720. That is a 10x collapse in credit per unit of emitted mass at IDENTICAL budget (0.0213 vs 0.2154). The README advertised +0.0100 (blocked holdout) and +0.0247 (live-anchored model) for this same artifact. Those two figures are a different frame and a model estimate respectively, so they are not the same measurement -- but neither was ever checked against the artifact's own internal consistency, and on that test it fails outright. SUPERSEDED 2026-10-04: the primary download is now gems32-heatfield-44090-cv-supconfined-zeros.tif (sha256 a84734ab532fffde...), a cross-validated field that beats the shipped artifact by +15.0% at matched mass under the whole-raster protocol. The defective file is retained on disk for the audit trail.
irregularities.mitigation: Root cause isolated and reproduced: the superseded rule smooths a 1-px binary ridge by sigma = 1.85 px and then runs a max-coverage greedy on the blur; smoothing lowers and SHIFTS the peak, so the sweep spreads mass over the blurred blob instead of locking onto the crest. Replaced by src/gems32/emitter.py: support-confined, lazy-greedy on the EXACT coverage-deducted marginal gain. Measured at matched 44,090-px budget: 0 off-support pixels, credit delivered on the field's own surface 90,230.9 vs the incumbent's 88,569.5 (+1.9%), and +0.1314 over the rule it replaces on the catalogue proxy. All six previously shipped files are demoted to comparators and the audit is reproducible with scripts/audit_shipped.py.

irregularities.statement: Two documents in this repository state DIFFERENT marginal bars for the same metric. src/gems32/metric.py and the passing test tests/test_metric.py::test_marginal_emission_rule_exact_single_truth_pixel say k > alpha*s = 0.0520 at s = 0.26. docs/research/score-ceiling-analysis.md section 1 states k > alpha*s/(1 - alpha*s) = 0.0549. The latter form does not follow from the metric: adding one unit of mass raises the denominator by EXACTLY alpha regardless of where it lands, giving k > alpha*s. A brute-force sweep over 300 random configurations agrees with the alpha*s form 300/300.
irregularities.mitigation: The exact theorem is stated, machine-verified in scripts/verify_theorems.py block (B), and used by src/gems32/emitter.py. NOTE the propagated consequence: the successor repository GEMSDOE28 uses tau_live = 0.05485 as its live break-even efficiency, which is 5.5% too high, biasing its pruning rule toward deleting dots that were still profitable.

irregularities.statement: The 'adaptive credit bar' that this project has repeatedly cited as its stopping rule CANNOT BIND on an emission confined to its own belief support. For a support pixel of a binary field, kbar(x) = sum_delta field(x+delta)k(delta) >= field(x)k(0) = 1, so the added false-positive mass 1 - kbar <= 0 and the acceptance inequality holds unconditionally for any s < 1/alpha = 5. Measured: emitter.emit(field, budget=None, prior_dti=0.26) consumes the ENTIRE 121,131-px H19-5 support and terminates with stopped_by='exhausted_support'.
irregularities.mitigation: Stated openly in knowledge/02 section 4b. The bar is still the correct rule for deciding whether a dot PAYS; it is simply not a constraint on an emission that never leaves its own support. Budget must therefore come from somewhere else -- which is exactly why the three-slot identification experiment that measures the hidden-set quantities is the next action rather than another budget sweep.

irregularities.statement: scripts/fetch_data.py's cache guard compared a file's sha256 TO ITSELF: 'hashlib.sha256(dest.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == _sha(dest)' is vacuously true, so any pre-existing file was accepted WITHOUT verification. A corrupted or truncated mirror would have been used silently.
irregularities.mitigation: The pinned digest is now passed into gh_raw(..., want_sha=...) so a stale file is re-fetched rather than trusted, and the post-fetch verification is unchanged. scripts/fetch_mirrors.sh is added as a fail-closed shell entry point that exits non-zero on any digest mismatch. irregularities.statement: The group's emission field is barely better than chance. Measured against the only truth in the checkout (labels.tif): a uniform-random 44,090-px emission scores DTI 0.078315 (5 seeds, range 0.077684-0.078960) while the group's dotted-d2.8 artifact at the same mass scores 0.161772 - a factor of 2.07. At 121,131 px the margin collapses: random 0.151988 vs the group's h19_5 field 0.166351, i.e. +9.4%. The field's support is 8.0% within 1 px of a mapped fault and 20.0% within 3 px, versus 3.55% and 8.56% for random support of the same size. The field is informative, but most of the emitted mass is spent where the kernel cannot reach it.
irregularities.mitigation: A 35-channel gradient-boosted field, cross-validated on four spatially blocked quadrants with a 30 px buffer, beats every shipped artifact at matched mass under two independent protocols (docs/research/hypotheses-round3.md, knowledge/02 section 13).

irregularities.statement: Emitted-mass optimum. Every informed field measured here peaks between 44,000 and 88,000 px and then loses score, because its ranking runs out of signal; a uniform-random emission has no ranking and keeps improving to 176,000 px, where it overtakes three of the five shipped artifacts. The previously shipped budget of 44,090 px sits just below the measured peak (88,000 px) under the whole-raster protocol.
irregularities.mitigation: Emit to the measured peak; the analytical stopping rule is the same bar as the marginal theorem - stop where the marginal expected kernel weight falls to alpha*DTI.

irregularities.statement: 13 of the 19 official bands have no derived channel in src/gems32/features.py (bands 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 16, 18, 19). Derived channels are built from only 6 bands (2, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17). Band 6 'tc' is the single most discriminative official band on the map (two-sided blocked AUC 0.5735, best of 19) and has no transform at all.
irregularities.mitigation: Round-3 hypotheses H62-1..5 address this; H62-1 was falsified on its own falsifier.

irregularities.statement: Hypothesis H62-1 (tilt-angle zero-crossing lineaments on band 6, the rank-1 candidate by univariate band ranking) was FALSIFIED by its own preregistered falsifier: ten transform variants were built (hard and soft zero-crossing locators and a negative Laplacian, each at sigma = 1.5, 3.0 and 6.0 px, plus a gradient magnitude). The best variant TIES the raw band (0.5737 vs 0.5736) and NOT ONE variant beats raw on all four spatial blocks; the textbook hard zero-crossing locator is worse than random (0.5058). The layer is already a derivative product, so re-differentiating it amplifies noise.
irregularities.mitigation: H62-4 (detrended-elevation curvature) rises to rank 1. The general law is recorded in docs/research/hypotheses-round3.md: transform only layers that are still raw fields.

irregularities.statement: Transform direction is layer-dependent and the repository applies it uniformly. Measured on four spatial blocks: the zero-crossing transform of det_elev gains +10.1% (0.5256 -> 0.5786) and of depth_to_base_surf gains +3.5% (0.5246 -> 0.5429), but the same transforms LOSE 0.04-0.06 on tc, 0.00-0.06 on geod_shearrate and 0.02-0.04 on geod_2ndinv. The repository's features.py docstring argues for replacing raw fields with line transforms as a general principle; that argument is measurably wrong for the strain-rate bands.
irregularities.mitigation: Use raw strain-rate layers (H62-3) and transform only the potential-field and subsurface field layers (H62-2, H62-4).

irregularities.statement: src/gems32/emission.py was dead in two places. _kernel_offsets() returns a 3-TUPLE OF ARRAYS, but coverage_credit() and greedy_cover() both wrote 'for dy, dx, k in _OFF', which iterates the three arrays and tries to unpack each one; for any footprint wider than 3 px this raises ValueError: too many values to unpack. Consequence: emission.greedy_cover -- the module's own REFERENCE greedy, the thing greedy_cover_fast is supposed to agree with -- could not run at all, so the fast path had never been checked against it. greedy_cover also used an inexact gain update ('coverage_credit * (1 - C)') that is not the metric's marginal gain.
irregularities.mitigation: Both call sites fixed to zip(*_OFF); added coverage_credit_residual() which computes the exact marginal gain sum_o f(x+o)*max(0, k(o) - C(x+o)) as a sum of shifted products; greedy_cover now uses it. After the fix greedy_cover and greedy_cover_fast produce BIT-IDENTICAL masks and identical objective values on all four test seeds.

irregularities.statement: The parallel-session rewrite of src/gems32/holdout.py deleted greedy_cover_adaptive while tests/test_emission.py still imported and used it, so the merged tree contained a test suite that could not pass against its own modules (27 failures at merge time). Related: paths.data_dir() did not look in data/raw/, which is where the fetched inputs actually land.
irregularities.mitigation: Tests re-pointed at the production pair emission.greedy_cover vs emission.greedy_cover_fast (a stronger test than the original, since it now exercises the shipped fast path); paths.data_dir() extended to search .cache/gems_data/, data/ and data/raw/. Full suite: 60 passed.

irregularities.statement: main's CI was RED before this merge (runs 37177047885 and 37177047887, both failure) because PR #7 added tests that depend on artifacts which are gitignored and were never committed: tests/test_gems32.py::test_all_12_submission_geotiffs_pass_range_01_audit requires docs/downloads/submissions_manifest.json plus 12 GeoTIFFs, and test_docs_and_readme_integrity requires the Core Values block and the portal-error string in docs/index.html, which scripts/build_site.py did not emit.
